stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist holds two patient referrals. One is written in indelible pencil. The other arrived by email as a flattened image which the pharmacy system can neither store nor retrieve in readable form. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pencil referral fails, because a paper document must be written in ink.
The emailed referral succeeds, because electronic transmission is permitted.
Both fail, because a referral must carry a handwritten signature to be valid.
The referral in indelible pencil satisfies the writing requirement.
The emailed referral fails the readable and retrievable requirement.

explanation.core_reasoning: 243 CMR 2.12(1) provides that references to written mean, if paper based, written in ink, indelible pencil or any other means; or transmitted electronically in a format that maintains patient confidentiality and can be read and stored in a retrievable and readable form. The paper route is deliberately permissive while the electronic route carries conditions the emailed image does not meet.

choice_analysis.A: Indelible pencil is named in the regulation alongside ink.
choice_analysis.B: Electronic transmission is permitted only on the stated conditions.
choice_analysis.C: Electronic signatures are expressly contemplated, so a handwritten signature is not essential.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: expressly within the paper limb.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: it can be neither read nor stored retrievably.

related_facts: Electronic transmission must also accord with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(g) and 105 CMR 721.00
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume the electronic document is the more compliant of the two because it looks more formal.

reasoning_steps: Classify each document as paper based or electronic
Apply the permissive paper limb to the first
Apply the confidentiality, readability and retrievability conditions to the second
